question: Which type of palace is deemed most excellent when the space between the two prior forms is divided?
premises: A palace is described as equal to a star.
This palace is designated as the best.
It is situated in the middle of the two previously mentioned forms when divided.
inference: The star-equal palace placed in the middle of the two prior forms is the most excellent option.
uncertainties: The exact referents of 'those two' depend on the preceding verses' architectural forms.
plain_english: When the space between those two is divided, a palace equal to a star, placed in the middle, is the best.
